title: How Does Your Body Feel Today?
caption: Feeling jittery today, with energy that pops then drops? Space is lively—fast solar wind and a strong south pull in Earth’s field are in play, so sensitivity can flare and focus may come in short clean runs. Keep it simple: try 3–5 minutes of slow breathing, step outside for a short break, and move easy.
snapshot: Geomagnetic conditions are unsettled, with a strong southward magnetic tilt holding. Solar wind is running fast. A minor flare showed up and a couple CMEs were observed, with no signs they’re aimed at us. Aurora chances stay on the low side over the next few days.
affects: A wired-and-tired pattern can show up as jittery energy with quick drop-offs. Focus may come in shorter clean stretches, then fade. Some people notice a restless body feel or a quicker pulse when standing up. Evenings may need gentler wind-down to avoid carrying the buzz into bedtime.
playbook:
- Use slow breathing for 3–5 minutes
- Take brief outdoor breaks and move easy
- Drink water and go lighter on caffeine
- Work in short, clear chunks with pauses
- Dim screens earlier than usual tonight

fb.caption:
How Does Your Body Feel Today? A little jittery, like energy pops and then drops, or focus only holds in short, clean bursts? Space is lively right now—fast solar wind and a steady southward tug on Earth’s magnetic field can turn up sensitivity, so some people may feel wired-and-tired or notice a quicker pulse on standing.

We also saw a small flare and a couple CMEs that don’t look aimed at us, so aurora odds stay low, but the background churn can still buzz the system. Try 3–5 minutes of slow breathing with longer exhales; it helps nudge the body out of “go” mode. Step outside for a brief walk and keep movement easy to bleed off extra charge without overtaxing. Drink water and go lighter on caffeine if you’re already shaky. Work in short, clearly defined chunks with a pause between, and dim screens earlier tonight so the alert feel doesn’t hitch a ride into bedtime.
